In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the superficial cell wall of the MAIS complex of mycobacteria is a peptidogylcolipid sheath.
the superficial cell wall layers of the smooth-colony-formers of the MAIS complex consist of peptidogycolipids.

the superficial layer of the cell wall of smooth MAIS serovars consists of an acetylated peptidoglycerolipid array, the structure of which has not been completely defined but which appears to be a serologically active, inert sheath that protects the pathogen within macrophage phagosomes from lysosomal hydrolytic enzymes.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
smooth-colony-formers are characterized by an outer cell wall sheath that is structurally related to the peptidoglican layer of Gram-positive bacteria.
the superficial cell wall layer in smooth-colony mycobacteria consists of a fibrillar array of peptidogylcoplipids, which is a novel cell wall component.
the cell wall of smooth-colony Mycobacterium is composed of three layers: a surface peptidogylcolipid layer, a middle peptidoglican layer, and a cytoplasmic membrane.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the cell surface of mycobacteria is much more complex than previously appreciated, and that the cell wall is a dynamic entity that is not static.

the superficial cell wall of MAIS is composed of a unique peptidoglycerolipid array that is structurally related to the peptidogycan of the cell wall of the mycobacteria but is chemically distinct from the peptidopolysaccharide of the mycobacterial cell wall.
the superficial cell wall layer of smooth-colony forming Mycobacteria consists of an array of acetylated C-myo-inositol 1-phosphate-lipopeptide peptidogycans.
